content.thinking:
I'm designing a kraken rising from water — a cthulhu-like squid head atop a torso with eight spread tentacles, sized so the mantle stands roughly 4 meters tall with tentacles spanning about 7 meters, tips touching the floor for ground contact.

I'm staging the pose: some tentacle undersides resting flat on the ground, others curling into the air, plus a shallow water-ring base disc with foam to anchor everything at y≈0. For the skeleton, I'm planning a hips root joint with a spine chain rising to the head, and tentacle chains parented off the hips/spine, each built as a skinned sweep.

For the palette, I'm going with an Overwatch-style bold, clean color-blocked look — deep teal/navy and purple body tones, coral suckers, cream-orange belly, with a single cyan glow accent, keeping flat colors within a 64-color limit while using paints like cel-shading and countershading sparingly.

Setting up imports and starting the hips joint and spine chain...

Simplifying the neck chain to a two-point path producing a single "neck" joint, then adding a separate "head" joint at the end aimed forward. Next I'm planning the torso sweep, building the body path with a catmull curve from hips upward.

Writing body paint logic...

For glow effects, I'm thinking I'll need decals with SVG textures — a glowing cyan rune swirl placed on the torso surface, positioned using the sweep's frame coordinates to put it on the front-facing side of the tube.

Now I'm designing the Cthulhu-like head: a scaled ellipsoid skull with a domed crest and fins, glowing cyan eyes as flat spheres, and a jointed jaw with upper beak and lower mandible parts. For the face tendrils, I'm planning four chains of three joints each using the tentacle role, sprouting near the mouth area.

Still shaping the crest outline...

Now I'm adding side head frills as fan-shaped extrusions in coral, and setting up glowing cyan almond-shaped eyes over dark sphere sockets.

Adjusting the brow ridge endpoints to sit correctly against the skull curvature, then moving to the mouth: setting a tendril origin point and planning the upper beak as a spike cone with a lower jaw hinged at a joint, aiming toward a forward point to form the jaw sweep.

Building out the tendril chains with curved paths tapering from jaw to tip, using unique names per segment and coral-to-cream color gradients, then moving on to the neck covering.

I'll go simpler and just capsule the neck directly instead of a full chain. For the shoulders I'm thinking pauldron-style armor plates, and I want to add dorsal fins along the spine using spike shapes swept along the torso's back axis, plus chest plating rows for extra detail.

Adding belly plates...

Now I'm planning the eight tentacles radiating from the hips, each rooted at a different azimuth around the lower torso, arcing outward and down toward the floor before curling the tip up into a spiral, with varying lengths and spread angles for a natural, asymmetric look.

Still tuning tentacle curl profiles...

I'm now mapping each tentacle type to its azimuth position around the body, spreading curl-type C (reaching down to floor) between the upward-arching B shapes for visual variety.

Let me rework the root cluster so it's hidden inside a larger lower torso sphere, with tentacle roots at radius 0.5 inside a 0.75-radius torso base. Each tentacle gets a 6-joint chain, keeping total joint count well under budget with 8 tentacles times 6 joints plus spine.

Computing world points for each tentacle path with proper azimuth placement, adding lateral sway via perpendicular offsets scaled by sine functions to create natural S-curve variation between tentacles, with tips curling inward in the radius-height plane.

I'm sweeping the tentacle geometry with a skin paint color and adding a coral underside sector for the sucker strip, then placing individual sucker discs along the underside at intervals, scaling each disc's radius to match the tentacle's taper.

With 8 tentacles times 14 suckers times 2 discs per sucker, I'm estimating around 224 parts for the suckers alone, totaling roughly 450 parts overall—well under the 1000 limit—so I'm defining a shared radius function to compute tentacle thickness consistently across all the sweep and sucker placements.

Now I'm thinking through sucker orientation: suckers should face the inner curve of each curled tentacle rather than a fixed world-down direction, since the clock angle along the tube path needs to track the curl plane so the suckers stay visible on the correct side whether the tentacle lies flat or curls upward.

Tracking which side of the tentacle faces the inside versus outside of the curl depends on the turning direction — for the outward-traveling curl the inside is the upper surface, but for B's arching motion which curls the opposite way (clockwise), the sucker side relationship flips.

I'll simplify by just picking reasonable sucker-facing angles for each tentacle type — roughly 55° for A and C (up and slightly toward travel) and 180° for B — rather than over-deriving exact geometry.

For shading, I'm sketching a tentacle color scheme that blends teal and purple with mottling, shifting gradually from a teal base near the body to purple near the tip using a gradient paint function.

Now I'm adding small dorsal spikes along the tentacles and glowing cyan runes as thin lines tracing partway down each tentacle for a signature visual detail.

I'm realizing sweep paths only follow the weight of the first bone they hit, so I need to specify `bone: chain` so the glow lines properly follow the whole tentacle chain. Instead of a continuous glow, I'll break it into a few dashed segments per tentacle to create a dotted luminous effect.

Now I'm figuring out placement details — small radius with round caps for the dots, slight lift so they sit on the surface, and different glow angles for the different tentacle variants (A/C vs B) relative to the suckers. I'm also setting up the torso sweep along the spine chain, defining radii as a function of position along the chain to shape the lower torso.

Adding a scaled teal skirt sphere at the hip base to hide the tentacle roots looks good. I'll skip giving it shoulder-mounted tentacles for simplicity and instead keep the standard eight, maybe adding a ring of small spikes around the shoulders for visual interest rather than full side fins.

Now I'm placing coral spike clusters at both shoulders, then building bevelled lathe-based shoulder armor plates with a cyan glow accent to give it that Overwatch-style look.

For the base, I'm sketching a water disc the tentacles rest on, but realizing the full tentacle spread would make the model too wide, so I need to scale down the reach to keep the overall footprint reasonable.

Adding ripple rings and splash droplets around the water base, merging the droplet spheres into one geometry for efficiency, then moving on to set up the hip bone at the origin.

For the mantle, I'm planning gill slit decals using a small cyan swirl SVG texture rasterized at low resolution, placed on the torso's chest areas while avoiding overlap with the glow line and plates down the front center.

Positioning symmetric decals on the sides of the torso, mirroring one across the axis, and figuring out the direction/size parameters for placement. For the head, I'm adding a glowing rune marking on the skull near the top front, working out the surface point and direction vectors needed to orient it correctly.

Checking imports to remove unused ones and making sure only the necessary utilities (THREE, builder, catmull, rng, glow, svg, cel, gradient, mottle, countershade, paint, mergeGeometries) are included, confirming types line up for radius functions and sweep chains. Now I'm defining the color palette constants for the body paint, picking teal, deep blue, and purple hex values to use with the mottle and cel shading functions.

Finalizing the belly versus body color split logic, settling on a cyan-forward palette with coral accents and using mottle plus cel shading to blend teal and deep tones for the torso's base coloring.

Now I'm working out tentacle gradients from root to tip blending teal into purple, building the paths with catmull curves, setting up sucker bands as angular sectors around each tentacle, and defining the sucker geometry itself as small cylinders placed along frames at specific angles.

Still writing geometry...

Still plotting tentacle coordinates...

Still working out tentacle geometry...

Now I'm working out the dorsal/gill fin shapes near the back of the torso, defining an extruded outline profile and figuring out where to position it relative to the spine and hips.

Still refining fin outline points...

I'm positioning the back fin at the torso's rear, with coral coloring and thickness settings, then defining the spine joint chain with coordinates progressing upward for the back segments.

Now I'm adding crown spikes around the head in symmetric pairs, placing a dark interior sphere for the mouth, and considering whether to skip gill details on the sides of the head.

For droplets, I'm merging small spheres scattered randomly in a ring near the tentacles to simulate a rising splash effect, keeping them floating above y=0.4 with varied sizes so they don't intersect, using around 40 instances with consistent sphere geometry.

Now I'm adding ripple tori oriented upward around the base for water rings, plus a foam skirt torus at the body's base, and realizing I need a lathe-shaped water mound to connect the torso visually to the water surface so it doesn't look like it's floating.

Checking the tentacle submersion depth against the water disc, keeping the minimum y just above the floor so it looks slightly sunk rather than clipping through. I'm settling on a cel-shaded toon style for consistency and defining the eye glow and tendril chain, laying out the jaw-parented tendril path points and their spread.

Working through the sweep function's types for the tendril and torso geometry, confirming the chain parameter accepts a string array and the paint fill works with the flat cyan glow sweeps. I'm placing the torso glow line along the front using a bone chain reference, checking where the plates attach on the torso surface.

The plates and spine glow line conflict at the same position, so I'm lifting the glow line slightly above the embedded plates to avoid overlap. For the head decals, I'm computing the frame placement and direction on the torso surface, texturing the rune decal with mirroring based on side, and making sure the glow material applies cleanly to the single-texture decal mesh.

For the eyes, I'm adding a small dark slit sphere scaled thin in front of the glowing eye sphere to form a pupil, positioning it just outside the main eye surface. Then I'm moving on to the skull's paint pattern, layering a mottled teal/deep base with a lighter patch near the face depending on surface normal and height.

Simplifying that face logic into a single mottled teal/purple head paint, and keeping the skull geometry as a low-segment cylinder for a flat, faceted look. Now I'm writing the file metadata — name, description, and style tagged "Overwatch" — before committing.

Writing tentacle generation loop...

Tuning sucker and glow angle placement so they don't overlap spike positions across the two tentacle types.

I'm reconsidering the torso spikes—they'd overlap with the dorsal sail fin, so I'll drop them and rely on the fin alone, adding shoulder spikes instead for extra detail.
